learningObjective: Explain how moving three bits from the fraction to the exponent gives BF16 FP32-like range but makes adjacent values near one eight times farther apart than FP16.
mediumRationale: Two aligned semantic tables are the smallest medium that exposes a fixed 16-bit budget, the competing exponent and fraction allocations, and one checkable consequence of each. Exact normal-range endpoints and next-after-one values connect abstract field widths to the underflow-versus-rounding failure modes.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Rejected because this is a quantitative allocation and spacing comparison, not a process or relationship topology; flowchart nodes would obscure the shared bit budget and exact values.
mediumComparison.svg: Rejected because fixed bit rectangles would either become too small at 390 CSS pixels or require horizontal scrolling. Real headings and tables provide the same alignment with better text reflow, selection, and assistive semantics.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Selected because two labelled panels align field widths with numerical consequences, stack into ordinary reading order below 640 CSS pixels, and preserve exact values without runtime rendering.
mediumComparison.interaction: Rejected because switching among all formats would hide states and add controls before the reader has formed the central FP16-versus-BF16 tradeoff. One deterministic comparison is sufficient.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected because the deck, official documentation, and papers contain related bit-layout figures, but no external artwork or paper-specific geometry is needed. The implementation uses original wording, values derived from the format definitions, and established site primitives.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected because the prose lists field widths and ranges but leaves readers to infer that a fixed total bit budget couples range and local spacing, and that reallocating three bits changes spacing by a factor of eight.

sourceReview.notes: The hardest prose-only mental model is that exponent width and fraction width buy different things from one fixed bit budget. For normal values in [1, 2), adjacent representable values differ by 2^(-fraction bits): FP16 spacing is 2^-10 and BF16 spacing is 2^-7, so BF16's gap is exactly eight times wider. Conversely, BF16's eight-bit exponent field gives normal magnitudes approximately 1.17549435e-38 through 3.38953139e38, while FP16's five-bit exponent field gives approximately 6.103515625e-5 through 65504. The visual states normal ranges explicitly because subnormal support and flush-to-zero behavior vary by format and hardware.

agentReview.summary: Read the complete article, text-indexed the full 214-page deck, rendered and inspected both relevant slide neighborhoods, and checked official NVIDIA, Google, and OCP documentation plus primary BF16 and FP8 papers before selecting an original semantic bit-budget comparison.

implementation.accessibility: The figure uses two semantic sections and real tables with scoped row and column headers. Format names, field counts, range endpoints, next-after-one values, and failure modes are all written explicitly; selected borders are redundant emphasis, so the lesson does not rely on color. The established two-panel primitive stacks below 640 CSS pixels with no minimum width and ordinary text wrapping, making it readable at 390 CSS pixels. Existing theme variables preserve dark-mode contrast, and shared print rules force a light high-contrast palette and avoid page breaks inside the figure.
